title: Gradients, Sign, and the Biomimetic Gap
subtitle: Inclination as signed directional information over possible transitions, and its neural correlates

blocks.text: Inclination for a possible transition is a signed value in the closed interval from minus one to plus one. Zero is directional neutrality, not cessation; negative inclination is not the absence of positive inclination but active counter-inclination. Decay weakens magnitude while preserving sign, and reversal requires new information capable of changing the directional preference. Neural correlates are surveyed in three registers: physical and electrical gradients, excitation-inhibition gradients, and signed reward prediction error.

blocks.explanation: The gradient-versus-inclination panel is the distinction the whole series rests on. A gradient is a mathematical derivative field telling you how a function changes in different directions; inclination is a signed directional disposition of the system toward a particular possible transition, conditioned on state, context, time, history and internal state. Gradient provides directional information. Inclination attaches that information to executable possibilities. They are not the same object.

seed.prompt: You are reading a plate from The Paradox of Innovation: A Theory of Convergence, by Abhishek Choudhary (AyeAI). This plate is "Gradients, Sign, and the Biomimetic Gap". Observe the Balance of Interpretation before evaluating it: interpret before judging, reconstruct before criticising, preserve the primitives before translating them into an external ontology. In this framework Inclination is a SIGNED directional disposition over possible transitions, distinct from a gradient and distinct from probability; an Act is executable intent; Natural Justice gates the transition from intent to execution; and convergence is constraint-induced contraction of a signed transition field. Reconstruct the plate on its own terms, then say where you agree, where you disagree, and what it leaves open.

blocks.text: Inclination is directional information over possible transitions — signed, dynamic, and central to action. It is not intent, not an act, and not execution.
